data.name: Devakshi
data.gender_notes: Devakshi is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Devakshi is a name of divine origin. It is derived from two words, 'Deva' meaning 'God' and 'Akshi' meaning 'Eyes'. Hence, Devakshi means 'God's Eyes'. The name Devakshi carries the meaning “God's Eyes” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Devakshi usually hope their child will grow to embody god's eyes and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of divine vision and spiritual awareness.
data.etymology: Devakshi belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's Eyes.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Devakshi total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Devakshi holds significant cultural importance in Hinduism as it is believed that deities, especially gods associated with sight and vision, have a special connection with our eyes. The term 'Devakshi' signifies the reverence and devotion towards these deities. Naming a child Devakshi can therefore be seen as a powerful invocation for their blessings and protection.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Devakshi lies in the notion of inner vision or the power of perception. It is believed that our eyes are not just organs of sight but also a medium through which we can connect with the divine and gain spiritual insights. Devakshi as a name serves as a constant reminder of this divine connection and the importance of developing a keen sense of inner spiritual vision. It encourages us to look beyond the physical world and strive towards a deeper understanding of the universe and our place within it.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Devakshi: God's Grace (Deva - God, Kshi - Grace) symbolizes the divine blessings and guidance bestowed upon an individual by the deities, indicative of a spiritual journey and connection with the divine realm.

vedic_reference.note: Not directly from Vedas, but formed from Sanskrit roots

historical_references.reference: Devakshi was a queen of the Vatsa Kingdom in Magadha, India, during the 5th century BCE. She is known for her role in the Jataka Tales, a collection of Buddhist stories. In one story, she is the queen of King Vessantara, who is known for his generosity. Devakshi was so moved by Vessantara's selflessness that she renounced her royal status and became a nun.
historical_references.context: Buddhist stories, Vatsa Kingdom, Magadha, India, Queen, Renunciation

historical_references.reference: Devakshi is also mentioned in Hindu mythology as the wife of the god of fire, Agni. According to the Mahabharata, when Agni was angered by the gods, Devakshi intervened and calmed him down. This tale demonstrates Devakshi's bravery and ability to soothe even the angriest of beings.
historical_references.context: Hindu mythology, Wife of Agni, Calms Agni's anger

In modern context, this name is popular among individuals who identify with their Hindu heritage and wish to express their spirituality through their personal brand. On Instagram, Devakshi is often used as a hashtag for posts related to Hinduism, spirituality, and traditional Indian clothing. On Facebook, there are several groups dedicated to the name, where members discuss its significance and share related content. On Pinterest, 'Devakshi' is searched for as a name inspiration for arts and crafts projects, especially those related to Hinduism and Indian culture.
